title: Log line built with an explicit CRLF in javascript — review required
description: A logging call in javascript concatenates an explicit carriage-return/line-feed pair into the message. A log processor that treats the event as one line will then show a forged second entry: an attacker who can influence the appended text writes whatever the operator later reads as a separate, trusted event. The rule matches the explicit CRLF in the call; it does not prove the value is attacker controlled.
remediation: Strip or encode CR and LF before logging, log structured fields instead of concatenated text, and configure the sink to escape control characters.
limitation: Lexical: matches explicit CRLF escapes inside common log calls; loggers that encode control characters internally are out of scope.
